BEHIND THE DEMO

A small game.
A look at how it works.

PixiJS draws the scene. GSAP brings the parts to life. Custom JavaScript gives every little friend weight, bounce, and a generous chance to come home.

Runs in your browserLayered PNG animationNo backendAI-assisted development

PIXIJS 8.22.0

The rendering

WebGL renders the ball, feet and claw as separate sprites. Containers provide pivots and hierarchy. Scene layers put the center finger behind the ball and the side fingers in front.

GSAP 3.15.0

The animation

Timelines coordinate the claw's travel and squeeze. Tweened transforms add squash, recovery and face crossfades. Each foot moves independently around its ankle.

The game systems

Custom JavaScript physics
A fixed 120 Hz simulation handles gravity, bounce, circle collisions and a damped spring grip. Catching is intentionally forgiving.
JavaScript ES modules
Game state, input, physics, visual rigs and interface are separate modules.
HTML, CSS & Web Audio
Responsive controls and overlays, with optional synthesized sound effects.

The development tools

OpenAI Codex
AI-assisted implementation, iteration, debugging and verification under the user's creative direction.
Node.js, npm & Git
Local preview, scripts, dependency management, tests and source history.
esbuild 0.28.2 & Prettier 3.9.10
Optional offline bundling and consistent source formatting.
Playwright & Google Chrome
Browser play checks and screenshots for visual review.

The artwork and the rig

The reference-based PNG exports and six expression layers were prepared earlier in the project conversation. The rig reuses those assets and moves individual parts with rotation, scaling and skew.

This produces a cutout-skeleton feel using PixiJS and GSAP. There is no Spine runtime, sprite-sheet animation, third-party physics engine, or live AI request during play.

A short demo introduction

“This is a client-side claw machine demo made with PixiJS and GSAP, with AI-assisted development using OpenAI Codex. The characters are assembled from separate PNG layers, so the feet and expressions can move independently. A custom physics solver gives the balls weight and bounce, with a forgiving grip. Everything is organized into small modules and packaged for GitHub Pages.”

Delivery and verification

GitHub Actions publishes the committed static game to GitHub Pages once the owner uploads the package and enables Pages. No server application or API keys are needed.

Development checks covered full-round play, controls, pause/reset, offline play and the updated character/claw composition. The repository includes six physics tests and syntax checks. The GitHub deployment must be verified after upload.
